figures.shows: A corner of the look-dev room, with a box on the left and a ball on the right of its floor, with ambient occlusion off and then on
figures.caption: The same corner of the room without and with ambient occlusion. With it, the floor under the ball, along the foot of the box and in the wall creases darkens.
figures.alt: Two pictures of a room corner with a grey box and a ball on a blue floor. In the second a soft dark patch lies under the ball, a thin dark band runs along the box's base, and the wall corner is darker.

figures.shows: The box and the ball of the look-dev room in the ambient occlusion view at the Low, Medium, High and Ultra rows
figures.caption: Every row darkens the same places. In front of the ball's foot, the floor's rings are strong on the low row, fainter on medium, a trace on high and absent on top. The low row also greys the open floor and the walls.
figures.alt: Four grey occlusion views of a box and a ball. In front of the ball's foot: strong rings, fainter rings, a trace, none. The first is greyer.

figures.shows: The look-dev room's west wall from beyond the west end, a box close to the lens, in the ambient occlusion view at intensity 3, with the radius at a quarter of a metre and at three metres
figures.caption: A radius of a quarter metre, then three, at intensity 3. The near box, held at the upper limit on screen, looks the same. At the foot of the room's west wall behind it, a thin dark line becomes a band.
figures.alt: Two grey occlusion views of a near box and a far white wall. The box's dark foot is the same in both; the wall's dark foot is wider in the second.
figures.numbers: The intensity is the recipe's figure-level component.set of PostProcess.AmbientOcclusionIntensity (3.0), which deepens the faint crease so it shows at page width; the radii are the variants' AmbientOcclusionRadius (0.25 and 3.0).

figures.shows: The look-dev poles, 3, 5 and 10 cm wide, against the ground far behind them, in the ambient occlusion view at Medium
figures.caption: Poles 3, 5 and 10 cm wide, left to right, against ground beyond the radius. Each leaves only a small dark mark at its foot, wider for thicker poles, and no outline along its shaft.
figures.alt: A grey occlusion view of three thin poles on a floor. Each has a small soft dark mark at its foot.
figures.numbers: The widths are the look-dev poles' scales (Pole 3cm, Pole 5cm, Pole 10cm at x 4, 5 and 6, Tools/LookDev/LookDevScene.json). The ground seen beside the shafts lies 2 m or more behind them, while the radius at the poles is held at the upper limit on screen, 12 % of 720 rows, about 0.3 m at 3.6 m with a fov of 36 degrees.

figures.shows: The lit look-dev room, with a box and a ball and ambient occlusion on, with TAA, with FXAA and with no anti-aliasing
figures.caption: The lit room with occlusion on, under TAA, under FXAA and with no anti-aliasing. The dark band at the foot of the box and the patch under the ball are the same in all three. Only the outlines differ: the occlusion needs no history.
figures.alt: Three pictures of a room with a grey box and a ball on a blue floor, which look the same: a soft dark band at the box's foot and a dark patch under the ball.

figures.shows: A slice through a pixel with its two horizons, the projected normal's angle and the cosine-weighted arc between the horizons
figures.caption: The slice is a plane through the pixel and the view direction. Two horizon lines leave the pixel, one for each side, and the arc between them is the part of the sky that the pixel sees.
figures.alt: A side view of a surface with a pixel on it, a normal arrow up, and two lines to the horizons with the arc between them shaded.

figures.shows: The 4x4 pattern as a grid of sixteen phases, and the five-tap tent over one row with its ends sharing a phase
figures.caption: Each block of four by four pixels holds every phase once. In a row of five taps, the two end taps fall on one phase and their half weights add up to a whole.
figures.alt: A grid of sixteen cells numbered by phase, and below it five bars of heights one half, one, one, one and one half; the end bars share a phase mark.

figures.shows: The horizon over six steps behind a pole and behind a board, with and without relaxation
figures.caption: Without relaxation the horizon stays at its highest sample. With it, the horizon behind the pole starts to fall two steps sooner and ends lower.
figures.alt: A line chart of the horizon against steps. One line stays flat without relaxation; two fall after the last high sample, the pole's lower than the board's.

figures.shows: The multi-bounce result against the visibility for albedos of 0.1, 0.4 and 0.8, with the radiosity means as dots
figures.caption: At every albedo the curve starts at the visibility and meets one at full visibility. A bright albedo lifts the curve far above the diagonal, and a dark albedo stays close to it.
figures.alt: A chart of the result against visibility, with a diagonal line and three curves above it, the brightest highest, and dots close to each curve.
